definition: Localized dilation or ballooning of a blood vessel, typically an artery, where the diameter increases by at least 50% compared to normal.
A disease process characterized by the buildup of plaque in arterial walls, leading to vessel narrowing and reduced blood flow.
A Doppler waveform pattern showing two distinct phases: forward flow during systole and brief reversed flow during early diastole, typical of peripheral arteries.
The widened area at the bifurcation of the common carotid artery into the internal and external carotid arteries.
Alternative pathways for blood flow that develop or become more prominent when primary vessels are obstructed or stenotic.
A ultrasound technique that displays blood flow direction and velocity as colored pixels superimposed on the grayscale image.
Formation of a blood clot (thrombus) in a deep vein, most commonly in the lower extremity veins.
Blood flow that occurs during the relaxation phase of the cardiac cycle, following systole.
Describes tissue or material that reflects ultrasound waves strongly, appearing bright or white on the ultrasound image.
The minimum velocity of blood flow at the end of diastole, just before the next systolic upstroke.
A vessel narrowing that results in altered blood flow patterns, typically requiring 50% or greater diameter reduction.
Increased blood flow to a tissue or organ, often seen as increased color Doppler signal.
A venous valve that fails to prevent retrograde (backward) blood flow, commonly seen in venous insufficiency.
The combined thickness of the intima and media layers of an arterial wall, used as a marker for atherosclerosis.
A Doppler waveform pattern showing a single phase of forward flow throughout the cardiac cycle, often indicating proximal obstruction.
The maximum velocity of blood flow during systole, used to assess stenosis severity.
Atherosclerotic buildup within arterial walls composed of lipids, cholesterol, calcium, and cellular debris.
The continuation of the femoral artery behind the knee, which bifurcates into the anterior and posterior tibial arteries.
A calculated ratio (PSV - EDV) / Mean Velocity that reflects peripheral vascular resistance.
Retrograde (backward) flow in veins lasting longer than 0.5-1.0 seconds, indicating venous valve incompetence.
A calculated ratio (PSV - EDV) / PSV that indicates downstream resistance, typically 0.6-0.8 in normal arteries.
Widening of the spectral Doppler waveform indicating turbulent flow, often seen at stenoses.
Abnormal narrowing of a blood vessel lumen, typically caused by atherosclerotic plaque or other pathology.
Blood flow that occurs during the contraction phase of the cardiac cycle.
A Doppler waveform pattern showing delayed systolic upstroke and reduced peak velocity, indicating proximal stenosis.
The formation of a blood clot (thrombus) within a blood vessel, obstructing blood flow.
A Doppler waveform showing three distinct phases: forward systolic flow, reversed early diastolic flow, and forward late diastolic flow.
A technique where the patient bears down or holds breath to increase intra-abdominal pressure, used to assess venous reflux.
Comparison of PSV at a stenosis to PSV in the normal vessel proximal to the stenosis, used to grade stenosis severity.
Impaired venous return due to incompetent valves, resulting in venous hypertension and reflux.
